experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass
experiences.description: Ski the world-famous slopes of Zermatt with stunning views of the Matterhorn. With over 360km of marked runs, this resort caters to all skill levels. Book slopes near the village base to maximize time after a late Day 1 arrival, starting fresh on Day 2. Stay in Zermatt village to walk to lifts each morning.

experiences.name: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking
experiences.description: Explore the breathtaking Jungfrau region on guided snowshoe trails through pristine alpine landscapes. Trails depart directly from Grindelwald village center, making it ideal for those staying locally. A perfect mid-week activity after ski days, requiring no special equipment rental beyond snowshoes included in the tour.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience
experiences.description: Skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz and optionally ride the historic Olympia Bob Run, one of the world's oldest natural ice bobsled tracks. Both attractions are within walking distance of St. Moritz village center, eliminating transfer time. Best enjoyed mid-afternoon when ice conditions are optimal.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening
experiences.description: Join a traditional Swiss fondue and raclette dinner experience in a historic mountain chalet in Verbier village. Learn about centuries-old Alpine cheese-making culture while warming up after a day on the slopes. Restaurants are clustered in the village center, perfect for guests staying in Verbier accommodations.

experiences.name: Glacier 3000 Cable Car & Snow Bus Adventure
experiences.description: Ride the iconic cable car to Glacier 3000 above Les Diablerets for panoramic views across four countries. Experience the Snow Bus ride across the glacier plateau and visit the Peak Walk suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks. The base station is a short walk from Les Diablerets village, ideal for a full afternoon excursion on a rest day from skiing.
